inference.tail_rule: One-tailed tests throughout (Table 3 and 4 notes). For HRM practice coefficients the tail is the hypothesized positive direction (negative HRM coefficients are never starred). For control variables the printed stars correspond to one-tailed tests in the direction of the estimate (negative controls are starred). Report t = coef/se and the one-tailed p in the direction of the estimate, plus the signed coefficient so either convention can be applied.
inference.joint_tests: Two incremental F-tests: (1) HRM block: F for the increase in R2 when the six HRM variables are added to the controls-plus-industry model (M2, M3, M7, M8; footnote c); (2) interaction block: F for the increase in R2 when the three interaction terms are added to the corresponding main-effects model (M4 vs M2, M5 vs M3, M9 vs M7, M10 vs M8; footnote d). Overall model F also reported. Degrees of freedom are not printed.

software_defaults: Software not stated. Assume ordinary least squares with conventional (homoskedastic) standard errors, unweighted, no clustering, intercept included, one industry group omitted; t-tests with residual degrees of freedom. Any package default reproduces this.
missingness: The article states no missing-data rule. User-missing codes per the dictionary (don't know, refused, not applicable; note that 997 for application counts and 4 'varies/depends' for training effectiveness are not declared missing and must be treated explicitly). Indices: averaging rule over structurally skipped or missing items is not stated (axis A04). Regressions: listwise deletion on the common variable set within each table is implied by identical N across models (axis A03). Record the number of cases lost at each step without reference to the article's printed N.
unresolved_items: Whether duplicate establishment records (V3 = 0) were dropped (A01).
Market performance subsample: profit-making (text) vs publicly held (Table 1 footnote) (A02).
Index construction when items are structurally skipped: mean of available items vs complete items (A04).
Staffing selectivity: log base, zero counts, codes 995/997 (A05); standardization sample (A06).
Training index: whether all three items are logged before standardization (Table 1 footnote b) or only standardized (text) (A07); values for establishments with no formal training (A08).
Decentralized decision making: mapping of NOS codes (head of org, someone below, larger org, combinations, depends) to the article's 1-5 scale (A10).
Subsidiary: V17 vs V21 and dummy orientation (A12).
Firm age: years (text) vs log (tables); zero-age handling (A13).
Total employment: full + part time vs NEWTOTAL vs full-time only (A14).
Percent managers: numerator when the manager block is skipped; denominator (A15).
Market competition: 1-4 scale (text) vs dummy (Table 2 descriptives, row label 'competitive pressure') (A16).
SIC two-digit coding from Census 1980 industry codes; number of groups (A17); crosswalk tie rules.
Interaction centering (A20); vertical hierarchy log base and top code (A21).
Treatment of V41 = 4 'neither' for product/service dummies (A23).
Software, covariance estimator and weighting are unstated; defaults assumed (A18, A19).
